name: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the cervix uteri
aliases: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the uterine cervix

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and immunohistochemical diagnostic criteria for adenoid cystic carcinoma of the cervix

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic cribriform, tubular, and solid growth patterns with basaloid cells and hyaline globules
Positive staining for cytokeratins, CD117 (c-KIT), and myoepithelial markers such as p63
Exclusion of other cervical carcinomas such as squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma by morphology and immunoprofile
Presentation with abnormal vaginal bleeding or cervical mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of characteristic growth patterns with supportive immunohistochemical profile and exclusion of other cervical carcinomas
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires biopsy and expert pathological review due to rarity and morphological overlap with other tumors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable cervical mass on pelvic examination

occasional.notes: Detected on imaging or physical exam

searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

rare.symptomName: Distant metastases symptoms (e.g., bone pain, respiratory symptoms)

searchTerms: swelling in legs due to lymph blockage
leg swelling from lymph fluid buildup

laboratory: Mild anemia on complete blood count
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing cervical mass with possible local invasion
CT scan for staging and detection of metastases
genetic: MYB-NFIB gene fusion reported in some cases of adenoid cystic carcinoma (rare in cervical cases)
other: Histopathology demonstrating cribriform and tubular patterns with hyaline globules
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD117 (c-KIT) and p63

distinguishingFeatures: Keratinization and intercellular bridges on histology
Positive p16 immunostaining associated with HPV infection
Basaloid morphology but lacks characteristic cribriform architecture

redFlags: Persistent abnormal vaginal bleeding unresponsive to treatment
Evidence of local invasion or distant metastases
references: Kurman RJ, Carcangiu ML, Herrington CS, Young RH. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 4th Edition. IARC; 2014.
Wang J, et al. Adenoid cystic carcinoma of the uterine cervix: a clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical study of 10 cases. Int J Gynecol Pathol. 2018.
